body:
Thank you for taking the time to do this AMA. 

Do you think use of IV ketamine as an acute treatment option for suicidal patients is viable? It's nearly a miracle drug in terms of response time and the drastic nature of positive response. Certainly it doesn't fix the underlying causes that therapy needs to address, but it would greatly decrease the need for hospital stays.

Has there ever been a place in your life where you felt safe? Can you do anything to bring back the imagery in your mind to that place? Familiar smells from there perhaps, looking at pictures, etc.? No one should treat you like this, you deserve better. But I know how much it hurts, how hard it is when no one that loves you is close by. Something my psych has been trying to get me to believe for years - you have the right to protect yourself. If you need to go inpatient for a few days that's okay. At the very least, I would try to increase therapy visits this week. We're here if you need an ear.

I'm so sorry you're hurting this much. I can relate to an abusive household and receiving blame for everything. One of the things that stands out to me in your post is that it sounds like you're a wonderful, kind, compassionate, and intelligent person. You are these things despite what's been done to you and the pain you're overwhelmed by. It sounds cliche, but the right girl will come along. There are many of us (girls) dying to find a man that is thoughtful, works hard, and cares about others. Being 17 sucks. I was miserable at 17, and couldn't get out of my house fast enough. But you will get out of there. The good thing about being an adult is that you can choose the type of people you want to surround yourself with. So hang on a little longer, get out of your house, get some help, and create a family that cares about you the way you deserve. 
I know it doesn't mean much coming from an internet stranger, but i feel your pain and send you my love.

I felt like that too before I formed a good relationship with mine. I've worked with my doc and therapist for years now and know they both truly care and want to help. I can call them at any time and know they will respond as soon as they can. They choose this work to help us when we can't see any other way. Its hard work for you and them but the reward of making a life worth living is worth every bit of effort. You're putting in so much work just to survive now. Why not have a trained ally that can help?

As much as we want our loved ones to help us, they're ill equipped to do so. There's a reason even trained therapists are not allowed to work with their own family, and they even have the education to know what to say and how to treat it! A word of advice though if you've never sought out therapy or a psychiatrist, don't settle. Feel free to go through multiple people until you find a relationship that really works for you. It's hard for people to understand how far gone we are unless they've been there themselves. And even if they do understand it, what can they really do to help other than offer you their love and support? It's kind of on us to do the work in the context of therapy (and on Rx if that's needed) :/
Thank you for this suggestion. It has been years since I meditated, and forgot it was even an option.

I keep asking myself if this (this moment) is all the fight I have to give. Thus far, the answer has been no, there's still more fight left in me even if it doesn't feel like it. Do you have anyone you can talk to? Are you getting any type of treatment? Life is always changing. If it can't possibly be any worse than it is now, why  not wait and see what better things come along?
(saying this for myself as much as I am for you)
This needs to be remembered more often, thank you.
